Official Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) guidance indicates a forecast maximum of 29°C under mostly cloudy skies, with a 30% chance of rain in the morning rising to 60% in the afternoon. Cloud cover and precipitation reduce surface heating and solar insolation, limiting the daily peak even as minimum temperatures hold near 25°C. Late-August climatology supports this outlook: average highs decline from roughly 29–30°C early in the month toward 27–28°C by the third week, consistent with the seasonal retreat of the monsoon ridge and increasing influence of transient frontal systems.

Recent model trends and the observed cooling since the July–early August peak (when extreme heat alerts covered Seoul) reinforce the market’s emphasis on the 27°C outcome. Traders are pricing in the likelihood that any brief clearing will not allow temperatures to reach or exceed 29°C, while the low probabilities assigned to 30°C+ or sub-26°C outcomes reflect the narrow uncertainty band around the KMA forecast and typical diurnal ranges for the region. Updated short-range guidance and afternoon observations on August 20 will be the key inputs likely to shift these probabilities before resolution.

Jeddah’s Red Sea location produces persistently high humidity that limits extreme daytime peaks compared with inland deserts, while the seasonal average August high sits near 37°C according to extended-range forecasts. Recent AccuWeather and regional outlooks show daily maxima between 35.4°C and 38.3°C through late August, with no strong signals of anomalous warming or cooling expected in the next 24–48 hours. Model consensus favors stable steering patterns and limited cloud cover, keeping the distribution narrow around these two bins while assigning lower probability to outliers below 36°C or at 39°C and above. Ensemble spread remains modest, with only limited upside to 16°C if afternoon insolation strengthens or a brief ridge builds.
